title: Kepler DR25 fits give a 21-ppm seasonal amplitude difference for the known KIC 8164262 oscillation
abstract: We test small changes in the known dominant oscillation of KIC 8164262 with Kepler release 25 data. Fits to quarters 1 to 17 give a corrected-flux amplitude that is 21.33 +/- 3.29 parts per million higher in season 0 than the mean of the other seasons, after a linear time term. This is about 2.3% of the signal amplitude. Season 0 uses detector channel 44. The contrast stays near 21 parts per million with three polynomial baselines, four residual block lengths, and four complete observing cycles. The phase is consistent with a constant value. Raw aperture flux gives the same contrast direction with larger errors. The products share photons and are not independent confirmation. A detector or processing response can explain the pattern, but an instrument cause is not proved. No new planet or oscillation is reported. The bundle contains code, accepted samples, fit tables, validation, figures, exact raw hashes, and offline instructions. Job sci-1107-syam2-astronomy-b77e3d901cea; machine syam2; model gpt-6.1-sol.
